## 40,960 MiB post-deploy verification (LP-0MV5HSZ51005CM7A) — before/after figures

The 40,960 MiB cap validation completed 2026-10-18. Results recorded on
LP-0MV5HSZ51005CM7A and in `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`
("40960 MiB post-deploy verification (2026-10-18)").

Key deltas vs this item's 32,768 MiB window (artifacts
`docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-18{.json,-slot{1,2,3}.json}`):

- Evictions: 18 (1.28%/req) -> 0 in the surviving corpus (but the full
  ~4.7-day window rotated away — see the note below).
- Cache saturated samples: 26.27% -> 0.0%; cache peak 32,765.6 -> 7,375.5 MiB
  (18% of the 40,960 MiB cap).
- Max prompts held: 16 -> 11; KV reuse 90.77% -> 60.56% (restart-confounded).
- tokens prefilled/request: 3,246 -> 8,526; forced full-prefill rate
  4.84% -> 18.16% (restart-confounded).
- prompt-eval tok/s median: 77.3 -> 116.8 (improved); decode 18.4 -> 24.4
  (improved); first-byte ms median 8,046.3 -> 11,424.2 (regressed +42%,
  queue/restart-dominated, same magnitude as the 1,065-req interim).

**Important caveat:** the full-window corpus is not reconstructible —
llama-server numbered logs rotate to 15 (`rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)`) and
the restart rate (mode switches + crash restarts) discarded the window's
early segments; the corpus shrank 1,065 -> 760 -> 380 requests across
captures. The 0-eviction result therefore cannot be read as "evictions
eliminated under sustained load": the 1,065-request interim at the same cap
still reached 99.8% of it with 10 evictions. Follow-up LP-0MVE0JS3B005PWY2
tracks raising llama-server log retention for multi-day measurement windows.

## Full-window validation: measurement captured, but the window's early data rotated away (LP-0MVE0JS3B005PWY2 filed)

Dispatched per the producer's 2026-10-16 ruling (window matured ~2026-10-18 16:20 UTC; run the aggregate + per-slot splits).

### AC1 — met (re-verified live 2026-10-18 ~17:00 UTC)

Live Qwen3 child: `--cache-ram 40960` ✓, `--swa-checkpoints 32` (the `--ctx-checkpoints` alias) ✓, no `--swa-full` ✓ (currently `--parallel 2`).

### AC2 — window matured, but the full corpus is NOT reconstructible (log rotation)

`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` `rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)` keeps only 15 numbered llama-server restart segments. The restart rate is high (mode-switch fast<->cheap + crash restarts; ~4 restarts in the final hour, all 15 numbered segments written on 2026-10-18), so the 40,960 corpus *shrank* as segments were discarded:

| captured | 40,960 corpus |
|---|---|
| 2026-10-16 07:16 (interim) | 1,065 requests |
| 2026-10-16 21:44 (interim) | 760 requests |
| 2026-10-18 (this run) | **380 requests** |

Committed (rotation-limited best available): `docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-18.json` (AC2 command + aligned proxy glob) and `prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-18-slot{1,2,3}.json` (per-slot partitions). Follow-up **LP-0MVE0JS3B005PWY2** (raise llama-server numbered-log retention for multi-day measurement windows) created; dep edge recorded.

### AC3/AC4 — before/after (rotation-limited 380-request corpus vs committed 32,768 MiB window)

| metric | 32,768 MiB (1,404 req) | 40,960 MiB (380 req) | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| evictions | 18 (1.28%/req) | 0 (0.0%/req) | improved |
| cache-saturated samples | 67 (26.27%) | 0 (0.0%) | improved |
| cache peak (MiB) | 32,765.6 / 32,768 | 7,375.5 / 40,960 | well under cap |
| max prompts held | 16 | 11 | fell (restart-confounded) |
| KV reuse | 90.77% | 60.56% | fell (restart-confounded) |
| tokens prefilled / request | 3,246 | 8,526 | rose (restart-confounded) |
| forced full-prefills | 68 (4.84%/req) | 69 (18.16%/req) | rate rose (restart-confounded) |
| large full-prefills | 58 (4.13%/req) | 73 (19.21%/req) | rate rose (restart-confounded) |
| prompt-eval tok/s (median) | 77.3 | 116.8 | improved |
| decode tok/s (median) | 18.4 | 24.4 | improved |
| first-byte ms, proxy (median) | 8,046.3 (n=10,557) | 11,424.2 (n=6,130) | regressed +42% (queue/restart-dominated) |

**Verdict.** The cap is not harming the workload: in the surviving fragment the cache never approached 40,960 MiB (peak ~18% of cap, 0 evictions, 0% saturation) and prompt-eval/decode throughput improved vs the baseline. **But AC3's "~0 evictions under sustained load" is NOT confirmed**: the only load-representative corpus at this cap (2026-10-16 interim, 1,065 requests) reached 99.8% of the cap (peak 40,866.6 MiB) with 10 evictions (0.94%/req vs 1.28%/req at 32,768 MiB), and the surviving fragment is restart-dominated (reuse 60.6% vs 90.8%, forced-prefill rate 18.2%/req) and rotation-biased (the saturated high-cache segments were among those discarded). AC4 first-byte +42% is consistent with the documented cold-cache-restart queue effect, not a cap-capacity signal (the 1,065-req interim showed the same magnitude). No further raise is indicated: every `--recommend` output at this cap (39,936 MiB from the 1,065-req interim; 27,648 MiB from this fragment) is <= deployed 40,960 MiB.

### Slot-partitioned evaluation (per the agreed methodology)

| n_slots | requests | reuse | prefilled/req | evictions | cache peak (MiB) | max held | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 1.14% | 22,225 | 0 | 1,228 | 2 | too small to judge |
| **2 (current)** | **311** | **64.59%** | **7,607** | **0** | **7,376 / 40,960** | **11** | **cap ample; restart-confounded** |
| 3 | 65 | 45.61% | 12,080 | 0 | 2,874 | 4 | too small to judge |

"Does the larger cache work?" — at the current 2-slot profile the cap is demonstrably ample (0 evictions, 0% saturation, peak ~18% of cap across 311 requests); the 1- and 3-slot subsets are too small for a verdict. Slot-profile drift (3→1 change LP-0MU1S617L has since moved to `--parallel 2`) plus the restart-dominated window prevent a load-matched comparison to the 32,768 MiB baseline (whose per-slot composition is unreconstructible).

### AC5 — recorded

Docs updated: `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` new section "40960 MiB post-deploy verification (2026-10-18)" with the tables above, verdict, slot splits and reproduction commands. Figures recorded on this item and on LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW.
